claim: A peer-reviewed October 16 Perspective proposes life-cycle-aware AI material discovery before material candidates are locked in.
verifiedFacts: The Perspective argues that manufacturing scalability, environmental impacts, product use and end-of-life are often evaluated too late.
This is a conceptual Perspective, not an experimentally verified industrial sustainability improvement.
inference: Inference: Fabrication optimization should include life-cycle uncertainty, not just physical or visual properties.
Consultancy implication and client problem: Life-cycle-aware material decision records: clients need early tradeoff visibility.
Project disposition and thesis: Shader Grammar CORE optical properties; Omni-Loom INCUBATE fabrication; extends sustainable material evaluation.
Actor roles: Researchers: Nature Sustainability authors; buyers: fabrication clients unverified.
significance: A peer-reviewed October 16 Perspective proposes life-cycle-aware AI material discovery before material candidates are locked in.
assumptions: Environmental claims may be made without trustworthy life-cycle inventories.
knownLimitations: Realistic cradle-to-grave LCA reverses the preferred material ranking.
